answer: To prevent sybil infiltration, an agent network can borrow the root-pruning logic of a drought-stressed cassava thread, limiting new identity nodes unless they prove deep resource investment. Just as a farmer discards a weak root vine under dry conditions to save the tuber, the protocol slashes untrusted agent accounts that fail continuous cryptographic challenges. This costly computational fertilizer requires attackers to burn massive stake per node, transforming cheap digital spam into a heavy pearly burden they cannot sustainably farm.
